description:
MATERIAL. Every mark in this collection is a square. Nothing else is drawn: no lines, no curves, no strokes, no glyphs. The squares are rotated at varying angles, scaled from a few pixels to nearly a quarter of the frame, and laid down with heavy alpha so they stack into deeper values where they overlap. There are exactly two colour populations and they never mix into a third: a warm amber/ochre family (roughly a dull gold, like brass or turmeric) and a cool slate blue-grey family, both sitting on a near-black ground that is very slightly blue.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Every one of the twelve is the same kind of object: a centred radial rosette. A warm amber core with n-fold rotational symmetry (I count 5-, 6- and 7-fold across the set) sits dead centre, and a field of cool grey squares drifts around it, thickening toward the corners and running off the frame edge. It reads to me as a coin or a medallion seen through falling ash; also as a rose window, a gear, a sunflower head, a splash frozen from above. The amber core is the subject and the grey field is weather. In the 512 single the reading is clearest: a lobed amber star with a serrated fringe of little amber cubes around its rim, floating in a slow grey snow.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. Centred composition, always. Radial symmetry, always. The same two-family palette, always. The square as the only mark, always. A dark gap or halo separating the amber core from the grey field in most of them (very pronounced in 1310661 and 1835793, where a clean black moat rings the core). Grey debris that is largest and densest at the corners and thins toward the centre.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Three axes, and they are strong. (1) SCALE of the core: 1203347, 1475115 and 1991107 are huge solid amber polygons filling more than half the frame; 1446330 and 1561509 are tiny, a small flower in a mostly empty black field; 1446330 in particular is almost an empty frame with a speck in it. (2) GRANULARITY: 1203347, 1475115, 1991107 and 1835793 are flat opaque slabs with clean silhouettes, whereas 1243682, 1283437 and 1561509 are built from hundreds of small squares and read as granular, fizzing, crumbling at the rim. (3) INVASION by the cool family: in most seeds the grey stays outside the core, but 1985692 is the outlier of the set - the grey squares lie ON TOP of the amber and take over the whole rosette, so the token reads cool grey with amber sparks trapped inside it. 1366079 is the halfway case: discrete dark squares sit inside the amber body like inclusions or holes punched in it.

MARKET STATES. Only four seeds are shown across states (1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661) and the change is enormous and unmistakable. NEUTRAL is the most reserved: compact core, clear black moat, grey debris kept to the periphery. STRESS is an explosion outward - the amber core roughly doubles, big amber squares fly out to and past the frame edges, the whole frame fills with overlapping gold, and in 1283437 and 1310661 a dense concentric mandala forms with a black hexagonal hole opening at the exact centre. STRESS is the brightest, largest, most golden and most ornate state of the three. RECOVERY sits between them but nearer neutral: the core is rounder and fuller than neutral, softened, with a scatter of small amber cubes orbiting the rim, and the grey field has withdrawn to the corners again. The direction of travel surprises me: the state named stress is the one that blooms.

AT 120px. It survives better than I expected, because the variation that carries is silhouette and mass rather than detail. The tiny sparse seeds (1446330, 1561509) and the grey-dominated one (1985692) are instantly distinguishable from the big solid ones. The fizzing rim of 1243682 and 1283437 still reads as a fuzzy edge versus the hard edge of 1310661. The weakness at this size is the three big solid seeds - 1203347, 1475115 and 1991107 - which collapse toward each other into 'a large amber polygon on black' and are hard to tell apart; their difference is only the number of points and its rotation. The interior detail of 1366079 (the dark inclusions) becomes mush. Across the state rows at 120px, the neutral-to-stress jump is obvious at a glance.

WHAT I NOTICE THAT MIGHT BE A PROBLEM. Every token is centred and none uses the frame differently; twelve bullseyes in a row. In the stress row the amber squares are cut hard by the frame edge (1203347 and 1243682 most visibly), which may be intended as overflow but reads as clipping. 1446330 is so empty it looks under-drawn rather than restrained. And in stress the object grows so much that the neutral and stress frames of 1203347 are close to being two different objects rather than one object in two moods.
